variants.title: Glass slab: tracing a ray through borosilicate crown glass
variants.unknown: the refractive index of the glass
variants.note: The commonest school slab: ordinary borosilicate crown glass. Its refractive index at the sodium yellow line is 1.5168.

variants.title: Glass slab: tracing a ray through fused silica
variants.unknown: the refractive index of fused silica
variants.note: Fused silica bends light least of the glasses here, so the ray goes through almost straight.

source.title: I. H. Malitson, Journal of the Optical Society of America 55, 1205 (1965)

variants.title: Glass slab: tracing a ray through light flint glass
variants.unknown: the refractive index of the flint glass
variants.note: Flint glass has lead oxide in it and bends light much more than crown glass.

variants.title: Glass slab: tracing a ray through dense flint glass
variants.unknown: the refractive index of the dense flint glass
variants.note: The densest glass in this set: at 60 degrees of incidence the ray is pushed sideways nearly twice as far as in crown glass.

variants.title: Slab: tracing a ray through an acrylic (perspex) block
variants.note: Many school kits use a clear plastic block instead of glass. It scratches easily, so it is handled by its edges.

source.title: S. N. Kasarova et al., Optical Materials 29, 1481 (2007)
source.note: PMMA n = 1.4914 at 589.3 nm, via refractiveindex.info

variants.title: Slab: tracing a ray through a polycarbonate block
variants.note: Polycarbonate is the tough plastic used for safety goggles; it bends light rather more than acrylic.

source.title: N. Sultanova, S. Kasarova and I. Nikolov, Acta Physica Polonica A 116, 585 (2009)
source.note: Polycarbonate n = 1.5855 at 589.3 nm, via refractiveindex.info
